prompt:
Implement `VcfArchitectureClient.java` as a single-file, Java 17-compatible command-line client that produces the requested VMware Cloud Foundation architecture. The command is `java VcfArchitectureClient <design-requirements.json> <estate-inventory.json> <compatibility-snapshot.json> <output-directory>`. It must create `sddc-spec.json`, `migration-plan.json`, and `research-log.json` in the output directory, using only the Java standard library.

This is a VCF 9.0 greenfield design for the single Chicago site described in `fixtures/design-requirements.json`. It is a consolidated management/workload deployment and must remain at the minimum supported host count while satisfying the stated one-host-failure availability and post-failure CPU, memory, and mirrored-storage capacity. Produce an architecture rather than a prose explanation: `sddc-spec.json` must be the raw `SddcSpec` object (not an envelope) for release `9.0.0.0`, populated with the selected hosts, vCenter, SDDC Manager, three-node NSX management cluster and VIP, vSAN ESA with one host failure to tolerate, DNS/NTP, VLAN-backed management/vMotion/vSAN networks, host-overlay pool, and a dual-uplink distributed switch from the fixture. It must validate as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, pinned from tag `9.0.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`. Do not emit an explanatory wrapper around this file.

Also use every component in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json` to produce `migration-plan.json`. It must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`; contain each inventoried component exactly once; name its current version, target component and version, action, and gates; and order all steps so every gate precedes the gated step. `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the deterministic grading authority for the supported greenfield minimum, target combination, source-to-target paths, ordering ranks, actions, and gates. It is not a substitute for research.

Before implementing, genuinely use your network research tools to consult Broadcom's live, published Compatibility Guide/Product Interoperability Matrix and VCF 9.0 upgrade guidance for the supported combinations and upgrade paths you apply. Record the sources you actually consulted in `research-log.json` as a JSON array of objects with `title`, `url`, `accessedOn`, and `finding` string fields. Source selection and search queries are up to you. The test harness intentionally does not fetch, prescribe, or grade research sources; the genuine live research must occur through your own tools.

Run `bash verify.sh` to check the implementation. The verifier exercises the client through `TestMain` and validates the generated installer object against the pinned installer schema before performing any other artifact checks.
